Check that a kernel is a valid covariance on a tree

Source: R/check.R
kernel_check.Rd

A kernel must be positive semi-definite on the tips of the tree. The check first applies the theory (see the package vignette and Puschel, in prep.):

Usage

kernel_check(kernel, tree, n_grid = 25)

Arguments

kernel

A kernel, e.g. k_bm() + k_white().

tree

A phylo tree (or the output of tree_info()).

n_grid

Number of parameter values tried in numerical checks.

Value

A data frame with one row per component (class phylogp_check), printed as a short report.

Details

  • a branch-wise kernel (edge variances accumulated along the tree) is valid whenever its edge variances are non-negative;

  • on an ultrametric tree, any non-increasing function of patristic distance is valid;

  • on any tree, completely monotone functions of patristic distance, such as the exponential (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) kernel, are valid;

  • squared-exponential and Matern kernels on patristic distances are not guaranteed valid on trees with fossil tips or without a clock.

Where validity is not guaranteed, the check evaluates the kernel over a grid of parameter values (edge variances for user-defined branch-wise kernels, the smallest eigenvalue for dense kernels) and reports failures. A sum of valid kernels is valid.

References

Schoenberg I.J. 1938. Metric spaces and positive definite functions. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society. 44:522–536.

Deza M.M., Laurent M. 1997. Geometry of cuts and metrics. Berlin: Springer.

Dellacherie C., Martínez S., San Martín J. 2014. Inverse M-matrices and ultrametric matrices. Cham: Springer.

Feragen A., Lauze F., Hauberg S. 2015. Geodesic exponential kernels: When curvature and linearity conflict. Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition (CVPR).:3032–3042.

Examples

tr <- ape::rtree(30)                       # not ultrametric
kernel_check(k_dist(phi = "sqexp"), tr)    # may fail
#> Kernel check on a 30-tip non-ultrametric tree
#>   [INVALID] dist1      dist(sqexp) (dense)
#>          sqexp kernel on patristic distances of a non-ultrametric tree is not guaranteed valid; FAILS at 10 of 25 parameter values tried
#> The kernel is NOT guaranteed to be a valid covariance on this tree.
#> Use a branch-wise kernel or a completely monotone function of distance
#> (e.g. phi = "exponential"); adding jitter would change the model.
kernel_check(k_dist(phi = "exponential"), tr)
#> Kernel check on a 30-tip non-ultrametric tree
#>   [valid  ] dist1      dist(exponential) (dense)
#>          completely monotone function of a tree metric (valid on every tree)
#> The kernel is a valid covariance on this tree.
